title: Locality-Sensitive Hashing (LSH)
interviewAnswer: LSH intentionally hashes similar items into the same buckets with high probability, reducing candidates for approximate similarity or nearest-neighbor search.
why: LSH explains scalable approximate search before modern graph indexes such as HNSW.
intuition: Normal hashing separates inputs; LSH wants similar inputs to collide.
deepDive: Different LSH families match different similarity measures; banding/concatenation tunes collision probability.
commonMistakes: Using a hash family for the wrong metric.
production: Benchmark recall, latency and memory together.
workedExample: Near-duplicate documents can be bucketed by MinHash signatures before exact checking.
